key_insight: Chronicle is an explainable transformer that learns from full, irregular cancer treatment timelines to continuously update risk predictions across many cancer types.
clinical_relevance: It may help clinicians stratify patient risk more accurately than single-snapshot models and support individualized decisions across different hospital systems.
method: Trained on 53.7 million longitudinal data points from 51,711 patients with 67 cancer types
Uses a transformer architecture that handles irregular timelines without imputation
Jointly predicts eight clinical endpoints with built-in explainability for patient-specific risk updates
evidence_signal: In the abstract, Chronicle outperformed cross-sectional models for overall survival (C-index 0.84 vs 0.76–0.79), predicted seven adverse event/transfusion outcomes with AUC 0.80–0.92, and generalized to 69,341 external patients across Germany, Switzerland, and the United States.
watch_item: Performance was reported from retrospective data, so real-world impact and workflow fit still need prospective validation before routine use.
paper_title: An explainable transformer model learning from entire treatment timelines for pan-cancer risk profiling across healthcare systems
